classification.difficultyReason: Read stationary points, an inflection point, increase and concavity directly from a supplied sketch.

content.prompt: The diagram to the right shows a curve $y=f(x)$. From the sketch find the values of $x$ for which:

spec.description: Qualitative coordinate sketch with intercept labels −2 and 4, minimum (−1, −2), maximum (2, 2), coordinate-label pointer arrows, and arrows on both curve ends. No equation is supplied; Bézier segments preserve the depicted relationships.
spec.mathematics: The curve decreases to x=−1, increases for −1<x<2, then decreases. Its concavity changes at the origin, from up to down.
spec.answerVisibility: All axes, intercept labels and turning-point coordinates are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.worked: The tangent is horizontal at the minimum and maximum, so $f'(x)=0$ at $x=-1$ and $x=2$.
The sketch changes concavity at the origin, where $f''(x)=0$. Thus $x=0$.
The curve rises from its minimum at $x=-1$ to its maximum at $x=2$, so it is increasing for $-1<x<2$.
The curve is concave up to the left of the origin, so $f''(x)>0$ for $x<0$.
